rows.note: This is the all-purpose choice for something intended for or concerning the community, including the general community-facing slice of sense 4.

example.jyutping: ni1 go3 hai6 gung1 gung6 tou4 syu1 gun2

rows.note: This is the all-purpose term for the public as the people in general, especially in notices and formal contexts.

example.english: The public is asked to note that filming will take place during the exhibition.
example.traditional: 請公眾留意，展覽期間場內會進行拍攝。
example.jyutping: cing2 gung1 zung3 lau4 ji3 zin2 laam5 kei4 gaan1 coeng4 noi6 wui5 zeon3 hang4 paak3 sip3

rows.note: Use this for the general public viewed as the masses rather than as members of a specific group.

example.english: This film is very popular with the public.
example.traditional: 呢套電影深受大眾歡迎。
example.jyutping: ni1 tou3 din6 jing2 sam1 sau6 daai6 zung3 fun1 jing4

rows.note: Use this when information or an action is openly visible or known rather than concealed.

example.english: The report has been made public.
example.jyutping: fan6 bou3 gou3 ji5 ging1 gung1 hoi1 zo2

rows.note: Use this for a particular public understood as the audience for a film, show, or other event.

example.english: The public said they were very moved after watching the show.
example.traditional: 觀眾睇完場戲都話好感動。
example.jyutping: gun1 zung3 tai2 jyun4 coeng4 hei3 dou1 waa6 hou2 gam2 dung6

rows.note: Use this specifically when an organization, service, or facility is operated or funded by the government rather than privately.

example.english: This public hospital charges low fees, so quite a few people go there.
example.traditional: 呢間公營醫院收費平，唔少人都去睇。
example.jyutping: ni1 gaan1 gung1 jing4 ji1 jyun2 sau1 fai3 peng4 m4 siu2 jan4 dou1 heoi3 tai2

rows.note: Use this for a public setting or the open, as in the phrase ‘in public’.

example.traditional: 你唔好喺公開場合鬧人。
example.jyutping: nei5 m4 hou2 hai2 gung1 hoi1 coeng4 hap6 naau6 jan4
